"I'm a big fan of Trello but I dread using Atlassian products... Hopefully Atlassian can learn from what makes Trello so wonderful instead of JIRA-ifying it into oblivion."
A fan of Trello complains about the "crippling 'add on' restrictions in Trello for solo users" and says removing them would be a huge win.
A user switched from Trello to Zenhub but says Trello is a really nice product that many people can use, not just people in software development.
"Trello is one of the best SaaS I've used."

A coworker who had set up Trello with a work email got a notice that the account was being migrated into an existing Atlassian account matching her email domain. Little information was provided, and the company has multiple Atlassian accounts, so they didn't know which one. The user called it "a weird janky process." Her only way out was switching to a different email address.

OP's story: they created a personal Trello account long before the Atlassian acquisition and later added a company email as a secondary address for a side project. Five years after leaving that company, the account stopped working one morning with no notification, and all their personal boards were gone.

Trello warned a user that an email on their account "belongs to an organization" and could become managed by that organization. The domain was actually the user's personal domain. They suspect any non-free email provider gets classified as a work address.

A user's Trello 2FA backup codes didn't work after changing countries and phones. Support's only offer was to delete all boards tied to their email and start fresh, losing 5 years of data across about 16 projects. They say they will never trust Atlassian with data again and moved to the open-source WeKan.
"Sad because it's my go to tool. It'll hold on for a while longer but at some point they will turn it into some sort of Jira Kanban+"
After this incident, a user who had been waiting "for the other shoe to drop since the Atlassian acquisition" is strongly reconsidering their Trello usage and asking where to migrate their data.
"I also found that Trello lacks some features and became too bloated over the years. NightReader plugin works well for darkmode, that's a plus."

Flipping a card over to see details fixes the user's main complaint with Pivotal Tracker, where everything is tiny and comment space is limited. "You could have a real discussion on the back of the card."
A user says everything is pretty intuitive except "vote," which is barely explained. They want the welcome board to include a card describing what voting is for.

The back of the card is very well done in the web app. However, the iPhone app is "very far from their web interface": it took 6-7 clicks to reach a checklist, making it "an order of magnitude less usable than their webapp."

Positives: Google login with a password option, and an awesome, responsive UI. Negatives: no pricing info. Also, creating a new board was slow to respond, so the user created another board and ended up with two boards of the same name. They suggested right-click menus and one-click labels.
A user who had searched for software matching their index-card to-do system said "This is perfect!" The only thing missing is an Android app.
A Trello member is automatically added to the user's first board, which makes them wonder if someone is reading their posts. It makes the board feel less private and trustworthy.

"Great app and highly intuitive." Signup was simple, and the starter board taught the user everything in 2 minutes. They love the card-back concept, the drag animations, and the easy "add people" feature. "A few well-done features instead of a thousand of useless and over complicated stuff... 10/10."
"This is exactly what I was looking for a long time for our content generation and feature implementation workflow. Idea board => Doing board => Done board."
The drag and drop has a nice effect, and the user sees it as a step up from Pivotal Tracker. They would like an installable paid version for internal company use.
